title: Launch Conductor: Cross-Surface Handoff & Stability Runway
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Context:
We need an accountable cross-surface runbook and orchestration plan that ensures clean handoffs between Runtime, Console, and API teams for feature releases that touch multiple surfaces (model routing, console rollout toggles, API contract changes). Past launches have shown gaps on 'day-of-go' escalation paths and surge decomposition (how to triage user traffic spikes when canary results are inconclusive). This ticket creates the Launch Conductor artifact: a single playbook, a timeline template for the launch calendar, and a lightweight automation checklist for day-of stabilization.

Goals (success criteria):
- Single source-of-truth launch artifact that all stakeholders can reference during preflight, rollout, and postmortem.
- Clear handoff points with owners for each runway segment (preflight, canary, scale, rollback).
- Defined surge decomposition steps to lower mean-time-to-recover for traffic incidents by 30% in the first two weeks post-launch.
- Rollout safety: automated guardrails (traffic caps, fast-fail thresholds, model-fallback mapping) in place and documented.
- Acceptance: at least 2 dry runs and stakeholder sign-offs from Runtime, Console, API, SRE, and Product before go-date.

Scope:
- Deliverables: Launch Conductor playbook (MD), templated calendar entries for cross-team cadences, Run-of-Show checklist, escalation roster, and a minimal automation script (GH Actions) to set/update canary toggles and create observability dashboards in Console.
- Out of scope: full on-call staffing changes and new infra procurement (those will be raised as separate ENG tickets).

Planned Timeline (high level):
- Week -4: Draft playbook + initial stakeholder review (Runtime, Console, API).
- Week -3: Integration dry run (canary toggles & metric dashboards) with SRE.
- Week -2: Full cross-team rehearsal (shadow traffic + rollback exercise).
- Week -1: Final signoffs and cutover freeze window defined.
- Day 0: Launch Conductor coordinates roll and monitors 6-hour critical window; surge decomposition yardstick used for triage.

Rollout / Canary strategy summary:
- Canary cohort: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated pause if latency or error budget breaches.
- Fast-fail thresholds:
  - 95th pct latency increase > 20% sustained for 3 minutes -> pause rollout.
  - Error rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline -> initiate rollback decision tree.
- Model fallback: runtime routes to last-known-stable model variant and decreases token budget for non-essential routes for 15 minutes during mitigation.

Escalation & Roles:
- Launch Lead (product): Ravi Kapoor (owner of this ticket).
- Runtime Lead (engineering): Maya Rivera.
- Console Lead (product/infra): Jonah Patel.
- API Contract Owner: Elena Martinez.
- SRE on-call (day-of): primary + secondary listed in Confluence roster (link below).
- Communications: #launch-bridge Slack channel and pre-populated incident snippets for external comms.

Metrics & Dashboards:
- Canary health dashboard (latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, success ratio, model-token cost) — template created in Console and linked.
- Post-launch metrics: user-facing latency SLA, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression alerts for top-10 prompt set.

Artifacts & Links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LAUNCH/Launch+Conductor+PRD
- Draft playbook (Google Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/launch-conductor/playbook-draft.md
- Canary automation GH Action (PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2048
- Canary dashboard template: console.redwood.ai/dashboard/launch-conductor-template

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should automated rollbacks be vs. manual operator intervention? Proposed: automated pause + 5-minute observation window, operator must explicitly approve rollback to reduce flapping risk.
- Granularity of traffic cohorts for API partners (some partners require bespoke canaries). We will include partner-scoped canary rules as optional extensions in the playbook.

Acceptance criteria (detailed):
- Playbook version v1.0 checked into Drive and linked in the launch calendar entry.
- Two dry-run rehearsals executed with notes and actions captured.
- Canary GH Action merged and validated in staging.
- Dashboard template available and imported into Console by SRE.
- Stakeholder signoff recorded (Runtime, Console, API, SRE, Security if required).

Next steps / immediate action items:
- (Ava) Share draft playbook with leads and schedule Week -4 review by 2026-02-27.
- (Ravi) Open PR for calendar automation and seed calendar slots for rehearsal windows.
- (Maya) Confirm required telemetry and add instrumentation tickets to ENG backlog.

notes: Use this ticket as the canonical preflight artifact for any cross-surface release that touches runtime routing, console toggles, or API surface changes. If the launch includes dedicated capacity SKU changes, create a child ENG ticket to capture capacity reservation and autoscaling validation.
